beats.text: Lost message? Lost ack? Crash? What can we promise?
beats.say: A message crosses the network. It can be lost, the acknowledgment can be lost, or the consumer can crash. So what can a system promise?

beats.text: At most once: send and forget. May lose.
beats.say: At most once: send and forget. If something fails the message is lost, but it is never duplicated.

beats.text: At least once: retry until acked. May duplicate.
beats.say: At least once: retry until acknowledged. Nothing is lost, but if the acknowledgment gets lost, the message arrives twice.
Exactly once is what everyone wants. In reality it is at-least-once delivery plus deduplication, so the effect happens only once.
In practice that means idempotent consumers, or transactions that commit the output and the offset together. Kafka offers both.

beats.text: Metrics, most systems, payments: pick by cost.
beats.say: Metrics can live with at-most-once. Most systems use at-least-once plus idempotency. Payments need exactly-once effects.
